500 grams ground beef. one onion. a cabbage, of course. as much rice whole wheat rice as you like. a can of peeled tomatoes. a bit of beef broth.

Add spices on the ground beef that you like. Set aside. I use salt, pepper, tumeric, onion powder, garlic powder, paprica powder and one I won't say. Next cook the rice. I do it a bit before I want to eat this, to let the water drain off better. Set aside. Add the beef broth and canned tomatoes in a pan together. Add some salt and pepper and whatever else you like to it to spice it up. Put on simmer. Chop up the onions and the cabbage. Brown the beef and add to the simmering tomato sauce. Drain if you want to be more healthy. Stir fry the cabbage and onion. Also add some spices to this while it's on the heat. Combine everything in a pot and let the flavors marry each other a bit before eating. Delicious. Perfect winter food. Inexpensive, easily done and amazing. You could add in some mushrooms if you feel like it. They go well with this too.
A cabbage recipe I came up with.

I cooked something similar for years. Let me see if I can remember.

Sautee one sweet onion and 2 cloves of garlic in the bottom of a sauce pan with some oil for about 7 minutes, or until it looks good. Then add half a pound of ground beef, salt and pepper. Stir until the beef is minimally browned on all outsides and add one small can of tomato paste and enough water so it does not burn (1-2 equal sized cans of water). Add the head of shredded cabbage and mix the crap out of it. Add a bit more water or broth, cover and stir occasionally. When the cabbage is a nice translucency then it is done.

It would probably turn out better cooking the ingredients separately and adding them like yours, but I like the one pot method for simplicity for a basic meal.

An alternative is to use a pre-shredded broccoli slaw and microwave it for 2-3 minutes before adding it to the pot instead of the cabbage. Mixes it up and is still really good.
